deities: Peddamma Thalli (Goddess of the Mother Goddess; worshipped as Santhana Lakshmi and as Mahishasura Mardini, eight-armed, Simha vahini)
festivals: Bonalu (Ashada Masam, June-July) - the temple's main festival; women carry decorated earthen pots with rice, jaggery, milk and curd as offerings

history.period: Modern - shrine dates back over a century (established 1908 per one account / more than 150 years per another); idol re-consecrated by Hampi Virupaksha Peetham pontiffs in 1984; Rajagopuram built 1993
history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: CSV row 2294 ('Peddamma Temple', Hyderabad, Telangana) is a confirmed duplicate of seq 983 ('Peddamma Temple', Secunderabad - id peddamma-temple-jubilee-hills). Both rows refer to the same temple: the famous Sri Peddamma Thalli Temple (Peddamma Gudi) at Road No. 55, CBI Colony, Jubilee Hills, Hyderabad - the best-known Peddamma temple and a major Bonalu centre in the twin cities. Deduplicate downstream; keep seq 983 as the primary record. (Identity note: Mahesh's brief for this batch names 'the famous Peddamma temple at Jubilee Hills', matching seq 983 exactly.) Legend: the Jubilee Hills area was once dense uninhabited forest; shepherds and farmers worshipped a small idol of the Goddess under a rock, and after the Goddess (in one telling) slayed the Asura she came here to quench her thirst at a well where a shepherd later found her idol. The shrine (established 1908 in a hut per one account; 150+ years old per others - conflict, verify) grew as Jubilee Hills developed in the 1990s, especially under the late P. Janardhan Reddy (PJR); the Rajagopuram was built in 1993 with a five-storey sanctum and seven-storey gopuram in Dravidian style. 'Peddamma' means 'mother of mothers'. A popular belief holds that a one-rupee coin standing upright at the base of the Dhvajasthambham signifies a granted wish. Research carried over from the primary record (seq 983); sources below are those consulted for that record.
